title: Paku Murah Bengkok Tiga Palu, Cap Keris Tetap Lurus
hook: Paku murah bengkok setelah tiga palu saat dipukul ke balok kayu keras
story: Di meja kerja bengkel kayu, kardus Paku Cap Keris sudah terbuka sejak frame pertama di sisi kanan meja. Tukang kayu memukul paku murah ke balok kayu keras dan paku itu melengkung setelah tiga pukulan. Ia membuang paku bengkok itu, mengambil paku Cap Keris yang lurus dan bersih dari kardus, lalu memukulnya ke balok yang sama sampai kepala paku rata tanpa bengkok. Ia menutup dengan menyuruh penonton menyimpan video sebelum belanja paku.
caption:
Paku murah sekali hantam langsung bengkok, kerja tukang jadi mundur. Paku Cap Keris dari PT Intan Suar Kartika tetap lurus waktu masuk balok kayu keras, spek lengkapnya tanya lewat DM.

shots.prompt: Photorealistic live-action video, vertical 9:16, 12 seconds, one continuous take, shot on smartphone vlog camera held at chest height with gentle natural handheld sway and a slight three-quarter angle down toward the wooden block, real daylight documentary look, natural clean daylight neutral white balance, true-to-life colors, realistic matte human skin with visible fine pores, no plastic shine, no waxy skin, no glass skin, no yellow or orange tint, no artificial golden glow, zero CGI, authentic non-AI documentary look, clean frame without camera HUD, no REC icon, no viewfinder brackets, no camera display overlay, no on-screen text or captions of any kind. Location: a simple wooden carpentry workshop bench in Medan, a thick dense hardwood block sits in the centre of the bench with fine sawdust on the surface, blurred stacked planks behind, bright overcast midday light from the open workshop door. At the right side of the bench, from the very first frame, one open brown kraft carton matching the single attached official reference photo stands upright, green print PAKU EXPORT QUALITY and CAP KERIS facing the camera, filled with loose clean shiny bulk steel nails without any plastic wrapping. An Indonesian male carpenter about 40 years old in a dusty dark grey long-sleeve work shirt, dark work trousers, brown cotton work gloves and a black field cap stands behind the bench; his face, gloved hands and torso stay in frame for the whole take. PROP CONTINUITY RULE: from 0.0s to 12.0s exactly one open nail carton on the right of the bench, one thick hardwood block in the centre, one hammer in his right hand, one short bent cheap nail already half-driven in the block and one straight nail taken from the carton are the only props; no second hammer, saw, chisel, bucket, wheelbarrow, vehicle, animal, extra person, extra carton may appear, move in, fall or disappear at any instant, and the carton print and nail thickness must not change. BEATS: at 0.0s he already swings the hammer down on the short cheap nail already set in the hardwood and after the third blow at about 2.4s the cheap nail is visibly bent sideways, while he says in calm unhurried Indonesian with accurate lip sync, "Paku murah sekali hantam bengkok". From 3.2s he pulls the bent nail out with the hammer claw, drops it on the bench, takes one straight shiny nail from the open carton and sets its tip on a fresh spot of the same hardwood block. From 5.0s he drives it in with four steady blows until the head sits flush with the wood, the nail shaft stays perfectly straight and does not bend or curl; he pauses about one second in silence and says calmly, "Paku Cap Keris PT Intan Suar Kartika tetap lurus". From 9.6s he taps the flush head once with light force, turns slightly toward the camera and pats the open carton with his gloved hand while saying, "Simpan dulu", then holds a small nod until 12.0s. Calm authoritative mandor tempo, roughly one and a half words per second, natural breathing pauses between the three spoken beats, real workshop ambience with hollow wood knocks and faint sawdust rustle, no music. Keep his face, clothing, gloves, cap, hardwood block and the open carton consistent throughout every frame.
